# Best Open-Ear Earbuds for Running (October 2026)

The major reviewers agree on a few top picks. Which one suits you depends on your budget, the weather you run in, and whether you want earbuds or a neckband.

| Pick | Price seen | Battery (buds / case) | Water rating | Best for |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Bose Ultra Open Earbuds** | $199 (list $299) | 7–7.5 h / 19.5–27 h | IPX4 | Best overall sound and fit |
| **Shokz OpenRun Pro 2** | $125–$180 | 12 h (neckband) | IP55 | Hearing traffic as clearly as possible |
| **Shokz OpenDots 2** | $200 | 10 h / 40 h | IP57 | Long runs and rain |
| **Soundcore AeroFit 2** | ~$80 | 10 h / 42 h | IP55 | Budget pick |
| **JLab Flex Open** | $40 | 7 h / 21 h | IP55 (per JLab) | Trying open-ear cheaply |

## The picks

**Bose Ultra Open Earbuds (best overall).** Runner's World's tester logged over 2,200 miles in them. They don't bounce, work with hats and glasses, and leak less sound than most open-ear designs. WIRED found their sound clearer than competitors' and liked the physical buttons for mid-run control. Downsides: only IPX4, so skip them if you run in heavy rain, and about 7 hours per charge. Runner's World also notes **Bose is expected to release a new open-ear model within about a month**, so it may be worth waiting if you're not in a hurry.
- Reviews: [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/) · [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/). Both pages have buy buttons for Bose, Amazon and Best Buy.

**Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 (best bone conduction).** This leaves your ears the most open, which is ideal for road running. It has 12-hour battery life, physical controls, USB-C, and an IP55 rating. RTINGS found it more rugged than the Bose. Downsides: the neckband can conflict with ponytails, hoods and high collars, and clarity is a bit behind the Bose. It was seen for $125 at REI, Best Buy and Walmart, compared with $180 at Amazon.
- Reviews: [WIRED review](https://www.wired.com/review/review-shokz-openrun-pro-2/) · [RTINGS Bose vs. Shokz comparison](https://www.rtings.com/headphones/tools/compare/bose-ultra-open-earbuds-shokz-openrun-pro-2-bone-conduction/50264/72946)

**Shokz OpenDots 2 (best for long runs and bad weather).** WIRED's overall top pick. It has 10 hours per charge, 40 hours with the case, IP57 (WIRED submerged it without problems), and wireless charging. One reviewer found the volume a little limited.
- Review: [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/), with links to Amazon, Best Buy and Shokz.

**Soundcore AeroFit 2 (best budget).** SoundGuys' budget pick. It has an ear-hook design that stays put, 10 hours of battery (42 with the case), IP55, and LDAC on Android. **Price note:** SoundGuys lists it at **$79.99 on Amazon**. That's cheaper than buying direct from Soundcore at $129.99, even with the coupon code AFSC20 ($104 after the code). The code also doesn't work on items already on sale.
- Review: [SoundGuys](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/), which has the Amazon link.
- To buy from Soundcore directly, a deal site lists it here: [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/go/soundcore-aerofit-2). This is an affiliate link.

**JLab Flex Open (cheapest way to try).** At $40, it's a low-risk way to see if you like clip-on open-ear earbuds. The trade-offs are weaker bass and touch-only controls. [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/)

## Quick advice
- **Busy roads, priority on awareness:** OpenRun Pro 2
- **Best sound, mostly dry weather:** Bose Ultra Open, or wait for Bose's new model
- **Marathon training or rainy climate:** OpenDots 2
- **Tight budget:** AeroFit 2 at about $80 on Amazon

If you tell me your budget, phone (iPhone or Android), and whether you wear glasses or hats, I can narrow this down to one pick.
